node: Specialty contractors tied to government-funded infrastructure, bases, ports, border, shipyards, depots, and secure facilities
summary: Layer 1B expanded the underfollowed lane for federal infrastructure specialty contractors. Reference anchors for later comparison include AECOM, Quanta Services, Fluor, Jacobs, and large defense primes, but this pass prioritizes smaller or less obvious public contractors where government-funded execution capacity, marine assets, skilled labor, project bonding, and customer qualification may matter more than headline policy exposure. The strongest underfollowed discovery signals in this pass are marine/dredging contractors tied to ports, Navy shipyards, USACE work, and civil contractors with high government-funded construction exposure. Key risk: low-margin contracting can convert policy-driven backlog into weak earnings if projects are misbid, delayed, disputed, or working-capital intensive.
